questions.q: What does the phrase 'To cry over spilt milk' mean?
o: To be very sad at a loss of money
To regret something that cannot be undone
questions.x: 'To cry over spilt milk' means: to regret something that cannot be undone.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: ABATE
questions.x: 'Abate' is the opposite of 'Intensify'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Abate'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: ASTUTE
questions.x: 'Astute' means shrewd. 'Naive' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To be a wet blanket'
o: To be a person who spoils others' fun
questions.x: 'To be a wet blanket' means: to be a person who spoils others' fun.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Spurious'.
questions.x: 'Spurious' is the opposite of 'Genuine'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Spurious'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: EXACERBATE
questions.x: 'Exacerbate' means worsen. 'Relieve' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: The minister's remarks were ____ to the issue under discussion; they did not address it at all.
questions.x: Correct answer: irrelevant. The second clause indicates the remarks were not related.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Wax'.
questions.x: 'Wax' is the opposite of 'Wane'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Wax'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
I would rather / you did not / share the password.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. Correct: 'would rather' + past tense for present preference about another person.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: JUBILANT
questions.x: 'Jubilant' means rejoicing. 'Mournful' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: The author describes a budget as:
o: A statement of priorities written in numbers
questions.x: Answer: 'A statement of priorities written in numbers'. This phrase opens the passage. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A budget is a statement of priorities written in numbers. When a government spends more on roads than on schools, it signals what it values, whether or not it says so in speeches. Citizens who learn to read budgets can ask sharper questions: how much was promised, how much was actually spent, and what was achieved. Transparency matters, but so does the capacity of citizens and legislators to interpret what is disclosed.

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the author's view on transparency?
o: Disclosure is useful only if people have the capacity to interpret it
questions.x: Answer: 'Disclosure is useful only if people have the capacity to interpret it'. The final sentence links transparency with the capacity to interpret. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A budget is a statement of priorities written in numbers. When a government spends more on roads than on schools, it signals what it values, whether or not it says so in speeches. Citizens who learn to read budgets can ask sharper questions: how much was promised, how much was actually spent, and what was achieved. Transparency matters, but so does the capacity of citizens and legislators to interpret what is disclosed.

questions.q: Who was the first and only Indian Governor-General of independent India?
questions.x: Correct answer: C. Rajagopalachari. He served from June 1948 to January 1950.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Indigo revolt (Neel Bidroh) broke out in Bengal.
questions.x: The Indigo revolt (Neel Bidroh) broke out in Bengal in 1859. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The Arms Act of 1878, which required Indians to obtain licences for arms while exempting Europeans, was passed under:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Lytton. It was resented as racially discriminatory.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It provided for provincial autonomy.
2. It provided for dyarchy at the Centre.
3. The All-India Federation it proposed came into being in 1937.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Federation never came into existence because princely states did not join.

questions.q: V. D. Savarkar described the Revolt of 1857 as:
o: The First War of Indian Independence
questions.x: Savarkar's 1909 book gave it that title; British historians called it a mutiny.

questions.q: The 1936 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Lucknow; it was a session at which Nehru advocated socialism as the goal.

questions.q: The book 'Unhappy India' was written by:
questions.x: 'Unhappy India' was written by Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.q: The newspaper/journal 'Jugantar' is associated with:
o: Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta
questions.x: 'Jugantar' was started/edited by Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1858:
1. It transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown.
2. It created the office of Secretary of State for India.
3. It introduced the system of dyarchy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Dyarchy came with the 1919 Act.

questions.q: The title 'Sardar' was conferred on Vallabhbhai Patel by the women of:
questions.x: After the successful Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Lamitiye' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Lamitiye' is a bilateral exercise between India and Seychelles.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Solar Alliance was launched by India and France.
2. Its headquarters is in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
The ISA was launched at COP21 in Paris (2015); its secretariat is at Gurugram.

questions.q: The 'IndiaAI Mission', approved in March 2024, includes:
o: Building AI compute capacity with thousands of GPUs and developing indigenous foundation models
questions.x: Correct answer: Building AI compute capacity with thousands of GPUs and developing indigenous foundation models. The outlay is about ₹10,372 crore.

questions.q: The 'Global Slavery Index' is published by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.x: 'Global Slavery Index' is brought out by Walk Free Foundation.

questions.q: The 'CPGRAMS' portal is used for:
o: Lodging public grievances with government departments
questions.x: It is run by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances.

questions.q: 'Mission Divyastra' (March 2024) was the first flight test of:
o: Agni-5 with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) technology
questions.x: Correct answer: Agni-5 with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) technology. MIRV allows one missile to hit several targets.

questions.q: Which team won its first IPL title in 2025?
questions.x: Correct answer: Royal Challengers Bengaluru. RCB defeated Punjab Kings in the final.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Universal Postal Union is located in:
questions.x: Universal Postal Union: headquartered in Bern.

questions.q: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 notably:
o: Implemented CITES provisions and rationalised schedules
questions.x: Correct answer: Implemented CITES provisions and rationalised schedules. It reduced six schedules to four.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 29 June?
o: National Science Day (discovery of the Raman effect)
National Statistics Day (birth anniversary of P. C. Mahalanobis)
questions.x: 29 June is National Statistics Day (birth anniversary of P. C. Mahalanobis).

questions.q: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly as its permanent President?
questions.x: Correct answer: Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary (provisional) chairman.

questions.q: The 18th Lok Sabha was constituted after the general elections held in:
questions.x: Om Birla was re-elected Speaker in June 2024.

questions.q: Article 214 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Facilities for instruction in mother tongue at primary stage
Raising the level of nutrition and public health; prohibition of intoxicating drinks
questions.x: Article 214: High Courts for States.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Governors of States"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 153.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission was set up under the:
questions.x: Correct answer: RTI Act, 2005. It hears second appeals and complaints under the RTI Act.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.x: She was appointed in 1989. Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court.

questions.q: Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) cardholders:
o: Have dual citizenship with full voting rights
Get lifelong visa-free travel but cannot vote or hold constitutional offices
Can be appointed judges of the Supreme Court
questions.x: India does not allow dual citizenship; OCI is a form of permanent residency status.

questions.q: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Legislators convicted of offences with a sentence of two years or more are disqualified immediately
questions.x: Section 8(4) of the RPA, which protected sitting legislators, was struck down.

questions.q: Article 21 has been interpreted to include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.x: The Supreme Court has repeatedly held there is no fundamental right to strike.

questions.q: The constitutional amendment that restored the power of States to prepare their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes was enacted in the year:
questions.x: This was the 105th Amendment Act, 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following items:
1. Remittances
2. Interest on external debt
3. FDI
4. Software exports
How many of the above are recorded in the current account of the Balance of Payments?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Remittances (transfers), interest (primary income) and software exports (services) are current account items; FDI is a capital/financial account item.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): Revenue receipts 21,000; Non-debt capital receipts 4,000; Revenue expenditure 47,000 (of which interest payments 12,000); Capital expenditure 13,000. The fiscal deficit is:
questions.x:
Total expenditure = 47,000 + 13,000 = 60,000.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts) = 60,000 − 25,000 = 35,000.
Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest = 23,000.
Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts = 26,000.
Answer (fiscal): ₹35,000 crore.

questions.q: The Unit Trust of India was set up — in which year?
questions.x: The Unit Trust of India was set up in 1964.

questions.q: India's target for non-fossil-fuel based electricity capacity by 2030 is:
questions.x: India announced the 500 GW target at COP26 (Glasgow) as part of 'Panchamrit'.

questions.q: 'Buffer stock' of foodgrains is maintained by the government mainly to:
o: Ensure food security and stabilise prices
questions.x: Correct answer: Ensure food security and stabilise prices. The FCI holds operational and strategic reserves.

questions.q: Which of the following is recorded in the current account of the BoP?
questions.x: Remittances are private transfers; FDI, FPI and ECBs are capital account items.

questions.q: "Doubling per capita income in ten years; monitorable targets" was the focus of which plan?
questions.x: It was the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–07).

questions.q: Under 'GST 2.0' reforms effective 22 September 2025, most goods fall under which main rate slabs?
questions.x: The GST Council rationalised the four-slab structure into two main slabs.

questions.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is significant because it:
o: Classified industries into three schedules with a dominant role for the public sector
questions.x: Correct answer: Classified industries into three schedules with a dominant role for the public sector. It is called the 'economic constitution' of India.

questions.q: The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) is associated with:
o: Comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households
questions.x: Nachiket Mor Committee (2013): Comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households.

questions.q: Specific donations received by a club for constructing a pavilion are:
o: Treated as income of the year
Credited to a separate fund and shown on the liabilities side
questions.x: Correct answer: Credited to a separate fund and shown on the liabilities side. Specific funds are used only for the stated purpose.

questions.q: Disclosing contingent liabilities in notes to accounts follows the convention of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Full disclosure. All information significant to users must be disclosed.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹45,000; Purchases ₹1,05,000; Purchase returns ₹1,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹1,42,000; Sales returns ₹3,000; Closing stock ₹65,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 45,000 + 1,05,000 − 1,000 + 3,000 − 65,000 = ₹87,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 1,42,000 − 3,000 − 87,000 = ₹52,000.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Repairs that significantly increase the life or capacity of an asset are:
o: Capital expenditure, debited to the asset
questions.x: Improvements enhancing future benefits are capitalised; routine repairs are revenue.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹47,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹250; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹600. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹47,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,000
− Bank charges 250
+ Interest credited 600
Pass book balance = ₹49,350.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,82,500; selling price ₹195 and variable cost ₹170 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹42,500?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (1,82,500 + 42,500) / 25 = 9,000 units.

questions.q: Abnormal loss of goods by theft is credited to the:
o: Trading account (and debited to P&L account, net of insurance claim)
questions.x: Correct answer: Trading account (and debited to P&L account, net of insurance claim). It is removed from trading results and shown as a loss in P&L.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹95,000, closing inventory is ₹90,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹7,40,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (95,000 + 90,000) / 2 = ₹92,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 7,40,000 / 92,500 = 8 times.

questions.q: The current ratio of a company is 3 : 1 and its working capital is ₹3,90,000. Its current assets amount to:
questions.x:
Let current liabilities = x. Then current assets = 3x and working capital = 3x − x = 2x.
2x = 3,90,000 → x = ₹1,95,000.
Current assets = 3 × 1,95,000 = ₹5,85,000.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹1,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 10% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 1,000 = ₹12,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 12,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹600.

questions.q: Ind AS 116 deals with:
questions.x: Ind AS 116 requires lessees to recognise right-of-use assets and lease liabilities.

questions.q: Opening entries, closing entries, adjustment and rectification entries are recorded in the:
questions.x: Transactions not fitting other subsidiary books go to the journal proper.

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹1,45,000 and at the end ₹1,97,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹30,000 and withdrew ₹2,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 1,97,500 + 2,500 − 30,000 − 1,45,000 = ₹25,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB) was set up in 2002 by:
o: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.x: GASAB formulates accounting standards for government (IGAS and IGFRS).

questions.q: In Workmen v. Reptakos Brett & Co. (1991), the Supreme Court added which component to the 15th ILC norms for minimum wage?
o: A bonus of one month's wage
A further 25% for children's education, medical needs, recreation, old age and marriage
questions.x: The Court held that 25% of the total minimum wage should cover children's education, medical requirements, recreation, festivals and provision for old age and marriage.

questions.q: An employer deducts 60% of a worker's wages for recovering an advance in one month. Under the Code on Wages, this is:
o: Not allowed, because total deductions cannot exceed 50% of wages
Allowed if the worker signs a consent form
questions.x: Correct answer: Not allowed, because total deductions cannot exceed 50% of wages. Section 18 caps total deductions at 50% of wages in any wage period.

questions.q: The Quarterly Employment Survey (QES) and the All-India Survey on Domestic Workers are conducted by:
questions.x: The Labour Bureau conducts establishment-based employment surveys including QES and surveys on migrant and domestic workers.

questions.q: The Supreme Court judgment in EPFO v. Sunil Kumar B. (November 2022) dealt mainly with:
o: Coverage of gig workers under ESI
The 2014 amendments to the Employees' Pension Scheme and the higher pension option
questions.x: The Court largely upheld the 2014 EPS amendments, struck down the requirement of contributing 1.16% extra by employees, and allowed eligible members to opt for higher pension.

questions.q: Under the bonus chapter of the Code on Wages, 'allocable surplus' for a company (other than a banking company) generally means what percentage of the available surplus?
questions.x: Allocable surplus is 67% of the available surplus for a company other than a banking company, and 60% in other cases.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, the term 'employee' for minimum wage purposes:
o: Includes managerial and supervisory staff as well as workers
questions.x: The Code's broad definition of employee covers all kinds of work for hire, so minimum wage applies universally.

questions.q: The IR Code's definition of 'strike' includes concerted casual leave taken on a given day by what proportion of the workers?
questions.x: Section 2(zl) includes concerted casual leave on a given day by 50% or more workers in the definition of strike.

questions.q: In Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management (1958), the Supreme Court interpreted 'any person' in the definition of industrial dispute to mean:
o: Only the members of a registered union
A person in whose employment or non-employment the workmen as a class have a direct and substantial interest
questions.x: The Court limited 'any person' to one in whom the workmen have a community of interest — here, an assistant medical officer was not such a person.

questions.q: Which body is the statutory authority for social security of building and other construction workers at the State level?
o: State Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board
questions.x: Each State has a BOCW Welfare Board that uses the cess fund for registered construction workers' welfare.

questions.q: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act was passed by the legislature in the year:
questions.x: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in 1979.

questions.q: The 1975 scheme of workers' participation in management, introduced during the Twenty-Point Programme, created:
o: Shop councils and joint councils in manufacturing and mining units
Works committees in all establishments with 20 workers
Worker directors in all private companies
questions.x: The 1975 scheme provided shop councils at the shop level and joint councils at the unit level in units employing 500 or more workers.

questions.q: The Royal Commission on Labour in India (1929–31) was chaired by:
questions.x: The Whitley Commission's report (1931) influenced later labour legislation including the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.

questions.q: Under the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008, the National Social Security Board was chaired by:
o: The Union Minister for Labour and Employment
questions.x: The National Board under the 2008 Act was chaired by the Union Labour Minister; the Code on Social Security continues a similar board.

questions.q:
Consider the following about safety officers and welfare officers under the OSH Code:
1. Thresholds for appointing safety officers are prescribed by the appropriate government.
2. The Code removed all requirements to appoint welfare officers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
The OSH Code retains welfare officer requirements (thresholds as prescribed) and safety officer requirements notified by the appropriate government.

questions.q: Workers of a company with 400 workers want to form a union. The minimum membership needed for registration under the IR Code is:
questions.x: 10% of 400 = 40; 100 workers — whichever is less → 40 (which is above the minimum of 7).

questions.q: The ILO's flagship report on social protection that found, for the first time, that more than half the world's population had at least one social protection benefit is:
questions.x: The World Social Protection Report 2024–26 found about 52% of the global population covered by at least one benefit.

questions.q: A landmark element of the 2019 Supreme Court judgment in the Vivekananda Vidyamandir case is that employers cannot:
o: Split wages into universally paid allowances to reduce EPF liability
questions.x: Allowances paid universally, necessarily and ordinarily to all employees are 'basic wages' for PF.

questions.q: Which country pioneered privatised, individually funded pension accounts in 1981?
questions.x: Chile's AFP system replaced PAYG with individual accounts managed by private funds.

questions.q: Atal Pension Yojana is administered by:
questions.x: APY uses NPS infrastructure; banks and post offices enrol subscribers.

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, ESI coverage for establishments with fewer than 10 employees is:
o: Voluntary, at the option of the employer and majority of employees
questions.x: Smaller establishments can opt in voluntarily; hazardous units can be mandatorily covered even with one employee.

questions.q: The 'Accessible India Campaign' (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan), launched in 2015, is related to:
o: Universal accessibility for persons with disabilities
questions.x: Correct answer: Universal accessibility for persons with disabilities. It targets accessible built environment, transport and ICT ecosystem.

questions.q: Which category of workers was brought under EPF coverage through the 'International Workers' provisions in 2008?
o: Foreign nationals working in India in covered establishments
questions.x: International workers (foreign nationals in India and Indians working in SSA countries) are covered under special provisions.

questions.q: Sweden's pension reform of the 1990s introduced a system in which contributions are recorded in individual accounts but benefits are financed on a PAYG basis. This is called a:
questions.x: NDC credits notional interest linked to economic growth while remaining PAYG-financed.

questions.q: 'Conditional cash transfer' programmes provide cash to beneficiaries:
o: Subject to conditions such as school attendance or health check-ups
questions.x: Correct answer: Subject to conditions such as school attendance or health check-ups. Examples include Janani Suraksha Yojana and Brazil's Bolsa Família.

questions.q: Gratuity under the Act must be paid within how many days of it becoming payable, failing which simple interest is payable?
questions.x: The employer must pay within 30 days; delay attracts simple interest.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹27,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 27,000 = ₹3,240.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 3,240 − 1,250 = ₹1,990.

questions.q: Under EPS 1995, if a member has no family, the monthly pension on the member's death is payable to:
questions.x: Correct answer: A nominee. Nominee pension is payable when the member has no eligible family.

questions.q: An employee retires after 18 years and 4 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹75,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
4 months is not more than six months, so it is ignored → 18 years.
= 15/26 × 75,000 × 18 = ₹7,78,846 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure hearing ability?
questions.x: Audiometer measures hearing ability.

questions.q: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) uses spectacles with:
questions.x: Correct answer: Concave lenses. Hypermetropia is corrected using convex lenses.

questions.q: In computing, 'FTP' stands for:
questions.x: FTP = File Transfer Protocol.

questions.q: Red blood cells are produced mainly in the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bone marrow. RBCs live about 120 days and carry oxygen via haemoglobin.

questions.q: The Excel formula =IF(B2>=40,"Pass","Fail") returns 'Pass' when B2 contains:
questions.x: The condition B2 ≥ 40 is true for 40.

questions.q: The chemical name/formula of 'blue vitriol' is:
questions.x: Blue vitriol = CuSO₄·5H₂O (copper sulphate).

questions.q: 'Bluetooth' is an example of a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Personal Area Network (PAN) technology. It works over short ranges.

questions.q: The causative agent of cholera is:
o: Dengue virus (a flavivirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes)
questions.x: Cholera: Vibrio cholerae (bacterium).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about vitamins:
1. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.
2. Vitamin C is stored in large amounts in the body.
3. Vitamin B12 is found mainly in animal foods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Water-soluble vitamins like C are not stored in large amounts and need regular intake.

questions.q: 'PM2.5' refers to:
o: Particulate matter with diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less
questions.x: Correct answer: Particulate matter with diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less. Fine particles penetrate deep into lungs.

questions.q: The causative agent of kala-azar is:
o: Chikungunya virus (an alphavirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes)
questions.x: Kala-azar: Leishmania donovani (protozoan, spread by sandflies).

questions.q: Cache memory is placed between:
questions.x: Correct answer: CPU and main memory. It stores frequently used data for faster access.

questions.q: The daily output of a cement plant rises by 50%, then falls by 25%, and finally rises by 5%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 50/100) × (1 − 25/100) × (1 + 5/100) = 1.5 × 0.75 × 1.05 = 1.1813.
Overall change = (1.1813 − 1) × 100 = 18.13% → 18.13% increase.
Note: simply adding (50 − 25 + 5) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 8 : 7 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 1. If each of them saves ₹10,125 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 8k, 7k and expenditures = 5m, 1m.
8k − 5m = 7k − 1m = 10,125 → 1k = 4m.
Solving gives k = 1,500, m = 375.
P's income = 8 × 1,500 = ₹12,000 (check: ₹12,000 − ₹1,875 = ₹10,125).

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 388, 910, 1084 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 910 − 388 = 522, 1084 − 910 = 174.
HCF(522, 174) = 174.

questions.q: An article is marked 80% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 180.
After 20%: 144; after a further 10%: 129.6.
Net = 129.6 − 100 = 29.6 → 29.6% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (20% + 10% ≠ 30%).

questions.q: ₹10,000 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 20/2 = 10%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 10,000 × (1 + 10/100)² = ₹12,100.
CI = ₹2,100 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹2,000).

questions.q: In a row, Deepak is 18th from the left and Vikram is 16th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Deepak becomes 29th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Deepak occupies Vikram's old place, which is 16th from the right and now 29th from the left.
Total = 29 + 16 − 1 = 44.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2019: 170  |  2020: 210  |  2021: 215  |  2022: 270  |  2023: 290.
What is the percentage change from 2021 to 2022?
questions.x:
Change = 270 − 215 = 55 on a base of 215 (earlier year).
% change = 55/215 × 100 = 25.58% → 25.58% increase.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹55,000. B joins after 8 months with ₹60,000, and C joins after 8 months with ₹40,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹31,800, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 55,000×12, B: 60,000×4, C: 40,000×4 → 33 : 12 : 8.
B's share = 12/53 × 31,800 = ₹7,200.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 130 m and 230 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.x:
Opposite directions → relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s.
Distance = sum of lengths = 360 m.
Time = 360 / 25 = 14.4 s.

questions.q: A vessel holds 25 litres of pure milk. 5 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 25 × (1 − 5/25)² = 25 × (0.8)² = 16 litres.
Removing 2 × 5 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 3^86 is divided by 7.
The absentee counts of a unit are: 46, 46, 30, 82, 53, 84, 22, 67, 18. Their arithmetic mean is:
questions.x: Sum = 448; number of values = 9. Mean = 448/9 = 49.78.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 8 : 7. After 14 years, the ratio will become 15 : 14. What is P's present age?

Gita starts from point O and walks 22 km towards North, then turns left and walks 9 km, then turns left and walks 26 km, and finally turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +22 -26 = -4 km → 4 km South.
East–West: -9 +12 = 3 km → 3 km East.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, towards South-East.
